record: dense Knowledge plan stability: six-execution plan class, custom versus generic plans, exact recall and latency at 1024 dimensions, and cached cleanup-authority routine plans
evidence_class: same-machine exact-role database benchmark on disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 fixtures with pgvector 0.8.7; synthetic clustered vectors; no release artifact, live embedding model, production hardware or other PostgreSQL major

method: Two tenants share the one partial HNSW index (93,390 indexed vectors across all tenants after ANALYZE). Each tenant holds clustered 1024-dimension vectors around 48 shared topic centroids in 30 projects, a workspace, the tenant root and a personal scope; 40% of items have a second revision and 10% a third, whose earlier vectors stay in the sidecar and graph; 5% are archived and 5% stale; 0.5% are session-sourced and half of those sources are withdrawn through the public route.
Corpora are created through ordinary tenant transactions under the runtime role, and withdrawals through the governed public API; VACUUM (ANALYZE) runs as the table owner before measurement.

Shapes: the context planner's exact scope chain (project, workspace, root, principal; about 13% of items, limit 96), one project's scope (about 3%, limit 96), public Knowledge search (no scope allowlist, limit 1,000) and the planner chain as known at a mid-seeding instant with history admitted (limit 96).

Each arm runs on a fresh single-connection pool: one untimed pass, then timed passes; ground truth is the same statement with enable_indexscan off. Plans come from EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) EXECUTE of a SQL-level PREPARE of the exact statement file, with the plan class read from pg_prepared_statements counters.

The six-execution study runs the unmodified product function six times on one connection and reads its plan class from pg_prepared_statements, then repeats six EXPLAIN EXECUTEs of an identical probe at plan_cache_mode auto.
findings: On the base commit the unmodified product statement switched from a custom to a generic plan at execution 6 on one pooled connection for 50,000-item broad search, and so did the identical probe (custom 7.6 to 8.2 s, generic 9.3 s). In the arm measurements the generic plan was slower in every shape, by 1.2 to 44 times, because it scans every current and historical head of the tenant.

No plan in any arm walked the HNSW index; every result was exact (recall@10 and recall@limit 1.0). With sorting disabled on a 4,000-item fixture the planner did choose the HNSW index and returned 17 of 1,000 requested rows, because a scan at ef_search 40 without iterative scanning stops before the tenant, scope and source filters run.

Rows behind withdrawn sources dominated cost: each called three LANGUAGE sql cleanup-authority routines that re-planned joins of up to eight tables, about 35 ms per such row; counting 6,041 revisions through RLS took about 860 ms with 20 withdrawn rows and about 120 ms after the routines cached their plans.

After the change the product statement is custom on all six executions in every shape and corpus, while the identical probe at plan_cache_mode auto still switches to generic at execution 6 for 50,000-item broad search (3.4 s against 2.1 s). Custom planning costs about 0.5 to 0.9 ms per execution.
The history shape contains no withdrawn-source rows and is the control: its latency is unchanged by the routine fix (10,000 items 61 ms to 59 ms p50).
limits: One Apple M5 Max host (18 cores, 36 GB) with OrbStack Docker 29.8.2 (18 vCPU, 16 GiB VM); PostgreSQL at fixture defaults (shared_buffers 128MB, work_mem 4MB, jit on). Figures apply to this host, PostgreSQL 17.11 and pgvector 0.8.7 only.
Synthetic clustered vectors, not BGE-M3 embeddings of real text; recall is exact by construction while the plan is exact, so it does not characterise approximate search.
Client wall-clock latency includes one loopback round trip to the container; the dense statement alone, not a ContextRun, is measured here.
Sample counts per arm are small (8 or 16 queries, 1 or 2 passes); p99 equals the maximum at these counts.
